core_obligations: Identify the complement (proof lines 15936-15939): since X' is dense, the complement Z = X minus X' has dimension zero, hence is a finite set of k-rational points x_1, ..., x_n.

Compute the cohomology of the sheaf supported on Z (proof lines 15940-15957): the short exact sequence 0 -> j_!j^{-1}F -> F -> i_*i^{-1}F -> 0 together with the vanishing of the higher direct images of the finite morphism i and the Leray spectral sequence gives H^q(X, i_*i^{-1}F) = H^q(Z, i^*F); since Z is a disjoint union of spectra of algebraically closed fields, these groups vanish for q > 0 and H^0 is the direct sum of the stalks F_{x_i}, each a finite Lambda-module because F is constructible.

Read off the equivalence from the long exact sequence (proof lines 15958-15968): the long exact cohomology sequence gives 0 -> H^0(X, j_!j^{-1}F) -> H^0(X, F) -> H^0(Z, i^{-1}F) -> H^1(X, j_!j^{-1}F) -> H^1(X, F) -> 0 together with isomorphisms H^q(X, j_!j^{-1}F) -> H^q(X, F) for q > 1; since the middle term is a finite Lambda-module, finiteness of the H^q(X, F) is equivalent to finiteness of the H^q(X, j_!j^{-1}F).
proof_roadmap: Note that the complement of a dense open in a curve of dimension at most one is a finite set of rational points.
Use the short exact sequence supported on that finite set and the Leray spectral sequence for the finite closed immersion to compute its cohomology.
Conclude the equivalence of finiteness from the resulting long exact sequence.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for a Noetherian ring Lambda, an algebraically closed field k, a separated finite type scheme X over k of dimension at most one, a constructible sheaf F of Lambda-modules on X_etale and the inclusion j : X' -> X of a dense open, the cohomology H^q(X, F) is a finite Lambda-module exactly when H^q(X, j_!j^{-1}F) is (statement lines 15926-15934). The proof (proof lines 15936-15970) identifies the complement as a finite set of rational points, computes the cohomology of the sheaf supported there through the Leray spectral sequence for the finite closed immersion, and reads the equivalence off the long exact sequence. H2: one exact sequence computation with two inputs, written out in full.
